BLOCKING FINDING: HPACStoreAuthority.complete_multi_write (src/pcae/core/hpac_foundation.py:739-758) never checks the capability's existing _spent / registry-CONSUMED state before spending it -- unlike require_writer and record_write in the same class, which explicitly defend against exactly this. Reproduced with fresh deterministic tests, not asserted: a second call to complete_multi_write on an already-completed capability does not raise, contradicting the method's own docstring claim of a fail-closed capability_stale rejection on a second call; 8 concurrent threads calling complete_multi_write on the same capability all 'succeed', with no exclusivity enforced at the completion boundary. This is a direct match to this phase's own listed BLOCKED trigger: '_multi_write weakens the verified one-operation / non-bearer semantics' (the spec's required invariant that one PAWA issuance authorizes at most one predeclared bounded multi-artifact transaction, not reusable writer authority). No other BLOCKED trigger in the phase's list fired. Fresh independent .1R.30R.3.5 IV suite added (tests/test_phase_149o_20l_7o_3w_1r_2b_1r_1_1r_30r_3_5_merged_rhamp_iv.py, 16 tests: 14 pass, 2 fail -- both failures are the exact finding above, deliberately left failing/uncorrected per this IV's own no-repair discipline).
